rules.title: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) – allowable annual rent increases
rules.requirement: For RSO units, rent may be raised only once every 12 months by the LAHD-published allowable rent increase percentage. Since February 2, 2026, landlords may no longer add an extra percentage for utilities, and the 10% increase for an added dependent is no longer allowed. A 10% increase for an added non-dependent tenant is still allowed within 60 days of learning of that tenant. Rent may reset to market only after a voluntary move-out, certain at-fault evictions, City Attorney-ordered evictions, or a buyout. Larger increases require LAHD approval (capital improvement, primary renovation, seismic retrofit, rehabilitation, just and reasonable return). Rent increases were frozen from March 30, 2020 through January 31, 2024.
rules.key_value: Once every 12 months by LAHD allowable percentage (no utilities add-on since 2026-02-02)
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, plus replacement units under LAMC 151.28. Covers apartments, duplexes, two or more single-family dwellings on one parcel, ADUs/JADUs, units attached to commercial buildings, long-stay hotel rooms and mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Rent is not regulated for condominium and townhome tenancies that began after December 31, 1995. A luxury exemption is available based on rents charged on or before May 31, 1978. Temporary exemptions may be filed with LAHD.
rules.interaction: Units not covered by the RSO may instead be subject to state rent cap rules (Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12), which are not described here.
rules.citation: L.A. Mun. Code ch. XV, art. 1

rules.title: Los Angeles RSO – legal reasons for eviction and relocation assistance
rules.requirement: Tenancies in RSO units may be terminated only for listed causes. At-fault causes: nonpayment, lease violation, nuisance/damage, illegal use, refusal to renew a similar agreement, denying access, and an unapproved subtenant at lease end. No-fault causes: owner or family move-in, resident manager move-in, demolition/removal from the rental market, government order, and conversion to affordable housing. No-fault evictions require relocation assistance, a Landlord Declaration of Intent to Evict filed with LAHD, and 30/60-day written notice (some require 120 days or up to a 1-year extension). All termination notices must be filed with LAHD within 3 business days of service.
rules.key_value: Eviction only for listed causes; relocation assistance required for no-fault evictions; notices filed with LAHD within 3 business days
rules.coverage_conditions: RSO units: properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, plus replacement units under LAMC 151.28.
rules.interaction: Non-RSO units are covered by the Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance instead.
rules.quoted_span: Give the tenant a 30-day and 60-day written notice (some evictions require 120-day notice or up to a 1-year extension).

rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (non-RSO units)
rules.requirement: Rental units not covered by the RSO have rights and responsibilities under the city's Just Cause Ordinance. Termination notices for covered units must be filed with LAHD within 3 business days of service (LAMC 165.05.B.5). The page does not detail the ordinance's specific causes or relocation amounts.
